title: Microshard-aware slab striping and adaptive spill buffer to reduce KV fragmentation and spillstorms
author: Ethan Mullins
description: Context: Hot tenants and mixed-size shard allocations cause repeated micro-fragmentation in the KV cache and periodic spillstorms when eviction rounds converge on the same slab ranges. This PR introduces two coordinated mitigations: 1) microshard-aware slab striping that scatters allocations for small hot objects across independent slab lanes to reduce local fragmentation and contention; 2) an adaptive spill buffer and anticipatory spill gating that temporarily absorbs eviction candidates and spreads downstream spill writes to avoid IO bursts. Motivation: in production SLOs we observed 95th percentile token latencies spike during cluster-wide compaction/eviction windows and a sustained 2x increase in spill IOPS under churn. Goals: reduce fragmentation-induced memory loss, smooth spill volume, lower p95/p99 latency jitter, and keep changes additive to the existing evictor interface. Design summary: - Slab striping: the slab allocator uses a tenant-aware microshard hash to choose a stripe index for small-size allocations (<512B). Each stripe has its own freelist and local allocation counters. The allocator prefers the local stripe before borrowing from neighbors. This reduces per-stripe fragmentation and hot-spotting. - Adaptive spill buffer: Eviction candidates are first placed into an in-memory ring buffer (bounded by a per-tenant budget). The buffer exposes three consumption modes: immediate-pass-through, paced-flush (rate-limited writer), and fallback-compact (when memory pressure is high). The spill policy dynamically transitions based on cluster-wide IO pressure and active eviction backlog. - Anticipatory gating: when eviction heuristics detect converging eviction windows (multiple workers selecting similar slab ranges) we apply a short randomized backoff and increase buffer pacing to avoid synchronized spillstorms. - Metrics and safety: new metrics for stripe occupancy, buffer fill, spill-pacer rate, and stalled-evictor-count. Safety nets include a hard-cap on buffer size and a bypass path to force immediate spill under out-of-memory signals. Implementation notes: - Modified src/runtime/kv/slab_allocator.{cc,h} to add stripe bookkeeping and a small constant-cost hash function. - Added src/runtime/kv/spill_buffer.{cc,h} implementing the ring buffer and pacing logic. - Updated src/runtime/kv/evictor_scheduler.{cc} to add cooperative gating and to consult stripe occupancy when choosing victim ranges. - Added benchmarks/kv/bench_spill.md and tests/kv/evictor_integration_test.cc to validate correctness and measure behavior under synthetic churn. Outcomes: lab and cluster tests show meaningful improvements: - 95th percentile token latency reduced by ~18% on high-churn workloads (synthetic tenant mix). - Measured memory fragmentation (lost bytes due to unusable holes) reduced by ~30% in long-running stress runs. - Average spill write volume during eviction windows reduced by 2.4x and peak IOPS smoothed by 60%. Backwards compatibility: no ABI changes to public runtime interfaces; the allocator hooks are additive. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated (kv.microshard_slab = on/off) with canary in a single region, monitor stripe occupancy and spill pacing metrics for two weeks before broader rollout. Related: follows on work from ENG-1982 (evictor pacing prototype) and is intended to be complementary to later generational reclaimer designs.
